name: Weavr
subtitle: Weavr for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV
description: Unsigned Weavr builds for iOS and tvOS. Add this source to Feather (or any AltStore-compatible signer) to install and update Weavr.

apps.name: Weavr iOS
apps.subtitle: 21 Nov 19:05 GMT · Multi-source IPTV with automatic failover
apps.localizedDescription: Weavr merges your M3U and Xtream sources into one library, removes duplicate channels and films across providers, and fails over to another source when a stream stalls. Includes a TV guide, films and series, continue watching, Picture in Picture, AirPlay, and WeavrLink, a remote for your Weavr TVs.

versions.localizedDescription:
Fetch missing and Merge again, from a source's page

- A media server's films and series: how many it says it has, kept as
  it's read, beside how many are stored ("Silo has 12,400: 600 missing").
- Fetch missing: the server read again with every title it gives kept and
  added to what's stored (none taken away, one already there passed over),
  so a big read that stops part way still brings in what it got; the
  library is made again if anything came. No "couldn't reach" or resting
  for a top-up.
- Merge again, when most of what a source has stored isn't in the library:
  the library made from what's stored, nothing asked of the sources.

A source's films and series as stored, on its own page

Settings > Sources > a source (on Apple TV, the source's menu > What's
stored): its films and series as its last complete read gave them, when
that was, and how many titles in the library carry it, so what's meant to
be there and what is can be seen side by side. A kind never read whole,
or read but with nothing from it in the library, shows in red.

Titles don't lose a copy when the library's made again; qualities asked again after a failed check

- A new library's rows are numbered on from the old one's. They reused
  the same numbers, and until the new index was read (seconds, for a big
  library) titles kept in memory still answered for those numbers: a
  film opened then (its details, its quality check, a Silo picture
  renewed) could have the old library's copy written over the new one,
  dropping a source's copy (Silo's) and its link for collections.
- A quality check of an Xtream or Jellyfin copy that got no answer (the
  panel busy, at its connection limit, timed out) is no longer remembered
  as "nothing to say": it's asked again next time, so the copy gets its
  quality instead of none for good.

Merging a big library no longer runs the phone out of memory

The merge (and bringing the old saved library in, and taking a source
out) runs as one long job, and each title read from the library file is
parsed with JSONSerialization, which leaves its objects for an
autorelease pool to free. Nothing drained one until the whole job ended,
so every title parsed and written stayed in memory: with a big Xtream
list and Silo, iOS ended the app part way through "Merging films and
series".
- Each merge batch, each saved piece brought in, each title of a source
  taken out, and each write of raw or merged titles now lets go of what
  it parsed and encoded as soon as it's done.
- Each merge batch notes how far it's got and the memory in use, so a
  run cut short says where in the log.

Silo: VLC takes over the same session, never two at once; why it failed, logged

When Apple's player turned down Silo's original, a second Silo session was
asked for VLC while the first was still being closed in the background;
Silo can refuse that (one stream at a time), and the title moved on to the
next source.
- Silo's original file: VLC plays the same session, no second one.
- Silo's copy for Apple's player (Dolby Vision): that session is closed,
  and waited for, before the original's asked for.
- The log says why Silo wouldn't start, and when VLC couldn't play it
  either, before the next source is tried.

Home's Sport row there from the start

The row fetched yesterday to a week ahead, one request per competition per
day, every launch (kept only in memory): often longer than the splash
waited, so it popped in after Home opened.
- Home's row fetches only yesterday, today and tomorrow (it shows what's
  live or on in the next day).
- Its last fixtures are kept between launches (a few hours) and shown at
  once, then fetched afresh behind; with none kept, the splash waits up
  to 8 seconds for them.

Quick Library and Watched buttons, sport ready with Home, faster expired pictures, centred splash text

- Library and Watched: a toggle re-marks only that title's rows (its
  index entries and what's kept of it), not the whole 190,000-title
  index with everything read cleared; and a title page reading from the
  library file now redraws when the library changes, so the button shows
  its new state at once.
- Home's Sport row is the app's own, fetched behind the splash ("Getting
  today's sport", up to 6 seconds) so it's there when Home opens; the row
  doesn't fetch it again.
- A Silo picture whose signature is known to have run out (its exp
  passed) has its title asked for afresh straight away, without the
  doomed request first; a couple more pictures load at once.
- The splash's line wraps, centred, when it's long.

Splash says what start-up is doing

The splash line follows start-up step by step instead of always saying
"Loading your home": Reading your channels, Updating your library for this
version (with how far, the first launch after this update), Reading your
films and series, Reading the TV guide, Checking your sources (then the
import panel if anything's fetched), Setting out Home.

Silo pictures that outlive their signature, Duo fixes, launch splash, sport cards, chips on TV

- Silo's picture addresses are signed and run out (daily, some every 15
  minutes; an expired one answers 404). Pictures are now kept by their
  identity without the signature, so one seen once is found under any
  later signature; an expired one with no copy has its title asked for
  afresh from Silo, its row given the new addresses, and loads.
- Collection covers come from Silo's collection list as it is now, not
  the signed address kept in the shelf. The shelf page has Refresh covers.
- Visible pictures are tried again after 2 and 8 seconds; an expired
  signature doesn't count against the server.
- Duo: no second search at the foot of the strip (the page's own top row
  has it); the side menu and headers follow the window as it folds and
  unfolds, so the menu no longer drops to the bottom after unfolding.
- The splash waits for the library to be read and, when it has to be
  fetched (nothing saved, or due), for that too.
- Shelf page: A to Z sorts by name without case or accents, the whole
  row tappable.
- Sport cards: team colours run darker over black, so a crest in its own
  colour stands out.
- Apple TV: filter chips (the log's among them) ringed and lifted when
  chosen, not swamped by the TV's white highlight.

Pictures kept on disk, whatever the server says, and folder posters remembered

- Every picture is saved to disk as it comes and shown from there on later
  launches, even with the server busy or unreachable, as the TV app's
  image cache does. Before, the system's cache kept only what a server
  allowed, and Silo's own pictures (collection covers among them) were
  fetched again each launch. A copy two weeks old is shown and quietly
  fetched afresh; past the limit (600 MB, 250 MB on Apple TV) the
  longest-unrefreshed go first. The old cache's room is given back.
- Each shelf folder's first four posters are remembered, so a folder
  without a picture of its own shows its square at once.

Server imports: Jellyfin and Emby read page by page, and failed pages tried again

- Jellyfin and Emby: each page of films or series is made into titles as
  it arrives, rather than the server's raw answer for the whole library
  being held until the end (too much for an Apple TV with a big library).
  Progress shows as it reads, as Silo's does.
- Jellyfin, Emby and Silo: a page that fails is tried twice more before
  the read gives up, so one slow answer among hundreds doesn't lose it.
- The log says why a page failed: the HTTP code or network error, and
  which of Jellyfin's routes it was on.

Very big servers on the Apple TV: each kind (films, then series) kept on disk the moment it's read, a few thousand titles to a file, never as one document (160,000 films made one bigger than the TV could hold, and it died writing it); a refresh cut short reads only what it hadn't kept; Silo's stretches let go as they're joined, and each source's titles once they're in the merge, so a big server isn't held twice

Sport: teams can be picked from any competition, not just the built-in ones — the extra competitions followed whole are listed under Teams, and More competitions… lists every one ESPN carries (searchable); a team ticked remembers its competition, so that competition's games are fetched; ticking teams no longer stops leagues followed whole from being fetched

Sport cards: one size for every card, nearer square (200 × 172 on the phone, 400 × 340 on the TV) — both teams always shown, one above the other, and a race or tournament the same size, with the sport's icon beside its name; league and time at the top, venue and channels at the foot
Duo: the side menu's gap at the foot the same as the strip's gap above its clock
